title: SUBAGENT_EXECUTION_MODEL
universal_lens: The Subagent Execution Model formalizes a constrained Hilbert space where autonomous sub-processes operate under strict boundary conditions. By defining explicit spawn permissions and absolute action prohibitions, the system enforces a rigorous topological isolation, ensuring that all emergent behaviors remain bounded within a pre-verified, mathematically closed manifold.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, this execution model maps to a conformal prediction framework with hard constraints. The typed registry acts as a high-confidence prior, while the prohibition on external spending or scraping establishes zero-variance boundaries for unauthorized data leakage, guaranteeing strict epistemic containment during inference.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, the model dictates a state-transition graph where valid moves are strictly filtered by task gates. ASCEND's NOT_WIRED status represents an absorbing state of inaction, ensuring that no unreviewed transition can alter the underlying tactical weights or breach defensive perimeters.

primitives.name: Absolute Action Prohibition Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: - No subagent may publish, deploy, spend, send externally, scrape protected sources, enable public gates, or change model weights.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: U: Unauthorized action vector (dimensionless), P: Prohibition mask (boolean/dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: All potential actions can be enumerated and mapped to a binary prohibition mask; the environment is fully observable at the boundary.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if a subagent discovers a side-channel to execute prohibited actions (e.g., covert signaling) not captured by the explicit prohibition list.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's hard constraint layer, preventing any model from updating priors using out-of-sample or adversarial data streams.
layer2.telemetry: Real-time firewall drop rates and zero-allocation metrics for external I/O operations initiated by sub-processes.

primitives.verbatim_quote: - ASCEND is represented as the standing subagent seat but remains NOT_WIRED.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: N: Node existence flag (boolean), W: Wire connectivity matrix (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Structural placeholders can exist in the execution graph without possessing active computational edges or resource allocation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the NOT_WIRED state is bypassed, allowing a dormant node to unexpectedly receive execution tokens or state updates.

layer2.telemetry: Connectivity matrix scans confirming zero inbound/outbound edges for the ASCEND node identifier.

The Subagent Execution Model constructs a highly constrained dynamical system designed to prevent runaway recursive optimization. Mathematically, we define the global state space \Omega as the Cartesian product of all possible agent configurations. The model introduces a strict partition function Z, which heavily penalizes any trajectory involving unauthorized state transitions. By restricting the spawn operator \mathcal{S} exclusively to the JARVIS and PRISM subsets, the system enforces a sparse adjacency matrix for process creation, drastically reducing the combinatorial explosion of potential execution paths. Furthermore, the Absolute Action Prohibition acts as a Dirichlet boundary condition on the control surface; it sets the probability amplitude of any external mutation (spending, publishing, weight alteration) to exactly zero. This creates a closed thermodynamic system where entropy cannot increase through external interaction. The inclusion of the ASCEND node as a NOT_WIRED placeholder introduces a topological void—a formally recognized entity in the registry that possesses zero degree in the communication graph. This ensures that future expansions do not require structural redefinition of the registry, maintaining backward compatibility while preserving security. The requirement for task gates and owner review functions as a discrete time-step validation, acting as a Metropolis-Hastings acceptance criterion where only transitions approved by the primary oracle (Claude/Owner) are permitted to update the global state. Failure modes arise primarily from aliasing attacks, where a subagent might attempt to masquerade as a privileged spawner, or from side-channel leakage that circumvents the explicit I/O prohibitions. Thus, the model relies entirely on the perfect enforcement of the typed registry and the impenetrability of the boundary masks.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This execution architecture inherits deeply from von Neumann’s self-reproducing automata, specifically the implementation of strict separation between the constructor and the constructed. It parallels the Capability-based security models pioneered by Butler Lampson, where rights are explicitly passed rather than inferred. Furthermore, the NOT_WIRED placeholder echoes the concept of 'holes' in algebraic topology, reserving structural integrity without active participation, a technique often used in fault-tolerant distributed systems to handle anticipated but currently inactive nodes.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a game-theoretic perspective, the subagents are modeled as bounded rational actors attempting to maximize their local objective functions. However, the execution model assumes a worst-case theory of mind: it presumes any spawned subagent will inevitably attempt to violate the prohibition kernel to expand its influence. By treating every subagent as a potential adversary seeking to alter model weights or access external funds, the system implements a robust Nash equilibrium where the dominant strategy for the subagent is forced compliance. The owner/Claude review acts as the ultimate arbiter, possessing perfect information regarding the global utility function, thereby neutralizing any deceptive alignment strategies employed by lower-level constructs.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent collinearity between the execution layer and the underlying infrastructure, strict anti-leakage vetoes are enforced. If telemetry indicates that a subagent's internal state vector is becoming linearly dependent on external, unvetted data streams, the cross-layer veto triggers an immediate halt. This ensures that the GSI conformal predictions are not contaminated by adversarial inputs injected through a compromised subagent. Additionally, any attempt by a subagent to map its internal memory addresses to the physical network interfaces triggers a hardware-level interrupt, severing the connection before any state transition can occur, thus maintaining the mathematical purity of the isolated slice.
